data.marketLevelRationale: The candidate is a fresh graduate with only a 6-month internship as a manual tester and two personal projects using HTML/CSS/JS. There is no professional development experience, no framework knowledge, and no demonstrated production-level work. This profile is firmly entry-level by any industry standard. The skill set is foundational, not specialized, and the experience volume is insufficient to qualify for even a junior designation without additional demonstrated competency.

salaryRange.note: Da Nang has a lower cost of living and smaller tech market than Ho Chi Minh City or Hanoi, which compresses entry-level salaries. Candidates with only HTML/CSS/basic JS and manual testing at the entry level typically fall in this range. Offers at the lower end are common for roles requiring only manual QA; offers toward the higher end require demonstrable front-end output. Do not expect the upper bound without a stronger portfolio.

coreStrengths.strength: Dual-track exposure in both QA and front-end development
coreStrengths.evidence: The candidate has a 6-month manual testing internship combined with personal projects in HTML/CSS/JS, giving them a broader perspective than peers who focus on only one discipline.
Two personal projects built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript demonstrate hands-on application of core web technologies beyond classroom theory.
The 6-month internship as a manual tester means the candidate has been exposed to bug reporting, test case execution, and software development lifecycles in a professional setting.
A College Diploma in IT provides structured technical grounding that aligns with both the QA and front-end paths the candidate has begun exploring.

criticalGaps.gap: No JavaScript framework or library proficiency
criticalGaps.impact: The vast majority of front-end job postings in Vietnam require React, Vue, or Angular. Without at least one framework, the candidate is ineligible for most front-end developer roles and will be filtered out at the screening stage.

Manual testing roles are shrinking and underpaid. Without Selenium, Playwright, Cypress, or similar tools, the candidate cannot progress in QA and will remain at the lowest tier of the testing career ladder.

The profile lists no target role, no target salary, and no stated interests. Without a clear path — QA engineer vs. front-end developer — skill development will remain scattered and the candidate will be outcompeted by peers with focused expertise.

Two personal projects with unspecified complexity, no live links mentioned, and no GitHub activity described provide weak evidence of competency. Employers in Da Nang at even the entry level expect demonstrable, reviewable work.

data.uniqueValueProposition: A dual-exposure entry-level candidate with hands-on grounding in both front-end development and software QA, positioned to become a well-rounded developer or test engineer if a focused skill path is committed to immediately.
data.readinessNote: The candidate meets the bare minimum threshold to apply for entry-level manual QA roles or junior HTML/CSS support positions, but lacks the framework knowledge, automation skills, portfolio depth, and career focus required to be competitive in the Da Nang tech market. A score above 50 would require at least one JavaScript framework project, a defined career target, and a stronger public portfolio. Current profile will result in limited callbacks and likely below-market offers.
